source_ref: ltm R package (CRAN) Mobility.Rd, read via tools::Rd_db("ltm"); data(Mobility) columns "Item 1" .. "Item 8"; upstream reference Bartholomew, Steel, Moustaki & Galbraith (2002) and Huq & Cleland (1990) BFS 1989
note: mapping_basis=paper_explicit: Mobility.Rd lists the eight activities under the headings "Item 1" .. "Item 8", which are literally the column names of data(Mobility), and the IRW codes are the number-preserving rename item_N. Checked against the data anyway (Step 5b route 1, verify_mobility.R): per-item endorsement counts reproduce the source colSums exactly for all 8 items (6745/2651/6349/3080/586/939/448/732) at n=8445 each, and the eight counts are pairwise distinct (min gap 138), so no permutation of the codes survives. text_source=translated_substitute because BFS 1989 interviewed rural Bangladeshi women and the administered wording was almost certainly Bengali, while the only wording published anywhere in scope is the ltm documentation's English; translation_source=third_party_english (the package documentation / Bartholomew et al. 2002, not the study's own materials, and not produced by this project). instructions is the documentation's third-person description with the coding legend moved to option_text, not verbatim administered instruction text. option_text "no"/"yes" is the Rd's own legend (1 = yes, 0 = no). No rights restriction locatable for these 1989 survey items; the redistributing package is GPL (>= 2).
public_note: The item wording for this table is the English text documented in the ltm R package, not the Bengali in which the Bangladesh Fertility Survey 1989 was administered to rural Bangladeshi women; no Bengali original is published in the source, and the instructions field is the documentation's description of what respondents were asked rather than a verbatim administered instruction.

(2025), figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.30385261, CC BY 4.0, file 'Moe SC ER demotivating styles.sav' (https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/58837756); processing script data/moe2025_selfcompassion.py.
note: PASS with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE: the sample is 95 Italian teachers (Moe, University of Padova; the .sav's Region codes run 1-10 for Italian regions) and the study will have administered an Italian ERQ, but the deposit is a single .sav that contains NO questionnaire text in any language -- every ERQ column has a NULL variable label and the file has no value labels at all -- and no article or supplement for this figshare 'dataset paper' could be located (searched for Moe 2025 self-compassion / demotivating styles / cognitive reappraisal; only earlier Moe & Katz papers surface). Recoverability is scoped to the deposit and the paper's own supplements, so this takes the SKILL Step-4 fallback: the canonical English ERQ goes in the base fields, language=Italian, the four _translated columns are empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. language=Italian is INFERRED from the sample, not stated in the deposit. Gross's own resources page does distribute an Italian ERQ (spl.stanford.edu/sites/g/files/sbiybj19321/files/media/file/italian.pdf); it is off-source for this deposit and there is nothing tying Moe's administration to that exact translation, so it was NOT shipped -- a later pass could substitute it if the administered version is ever confirmed. (2) MAPPING: the .sav gives no labels, so the code->text tie is the canonical instrument's own printed item numbers 1-10 against codes ERQ1_pre..ERQ10_pre -- NOT a code list published by Moe (2025). Checked against the data via the .sav's own derived Reappraisal composite; see verify_moe2025_erq.R and the verification row (PARTIAL: pins the reappraisal/suppression partition exactly, not order within a subscale). (3) OPTION TEXT: the ERQ prints anchors only at 1 'strongly disagree', 4 'neutral' and 7 'strongly agree'; points 2, 3, 5 and 6 are unlabelled on the form and are left blank rather than padded. (4) RIGHTS: no fee, permission requirement, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause. The only term on the source page (spl.stanford.edu/resources, sha256 93f7a3a970822fa4d495ad062f8b111edbccceb46515037df5d47ebf9cb8aabd, fetched 2026-09-09) is "The measures provided here may be used for academic research purposes with appropriate citation.", and the ERQ from this page was ruled shippable by ben-domingue on 2026-09-08 (irw#2121, li_2024_bdyz: "ships Gross & John's (2003) English ERQ wording, which Gross distributes freely from his own lab page, so it ships"). Applied, not re-derived. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: instrument_rights_register.csv carries no ERQ row -- one could be added with verdict=ship on that ruling. (5) The deposit itself is CC BY 4.0 (figshare 30385261).
public_note: The ERQ was administered to Italian teachers, but the figshare deposit is a single SPSS file with no item wording in any language and no accompanying article or supplement could be located, so the item text shown here is Gross & John's (2003) canonical English ERQ rather than the Italian sentences the teachers read. Item codes ERQ1_pre-ERQ10_pre are matched to the instrument's own printed item numbers; the assignment of reappraisal versus suppression wording is confirmed by the deposit's own Reappraisal composite, which is the mean of exactly ERQ1/3/5/7/8/10 (the unique such six-item subset of 210, next-best deviation 0.83), but nothing in the data distinguishes the near-parallel reappraisal items 1, 3, 7 and 10 from one another. Scale points 2, 3, 5 and 6 carry no option text because the ERQ form labels only 1, 4 and 7.

note: Instrument identified from the live data, not the table name: 26 items on a 1-5 scale with the .sav's reverse-key duplicate set {1,2,4,6,8,11,13,16,18,20,21,24,25} identical to Neff's SCS-26 scoring key -- Self-Compassion Scale, not Self-Control/Social Connectedness. Item codes SCS1_pre..SCS26_pre are the .sav's own column names (data/moe2025_selfcompassion.py selects raw.columns starting 'SCS' and excluding '_rev'), so no positional assignment is involved; the codes' numbers are tied to item_text by the explicit 1-26 numbering printed in the instrument PDFs. Italian wording verbatim from ItalianSCS.pdf (sha256 bbe4585b...05e05c6), English twin verbatim from SCS-information.pdf (sha256 be9f7f47...acdaabc752a), both fetched 2026-09-09 from self-compassion.org. RIGHTS: the SCS information sheet on the rights holder's own site states 'Dr. Kristin Neff grants permission to use the Self-Compassion Scale (Neff, 2003) for any purpose whatsoever, including research, clinical work, teaching, etc.' and 'Permission is also given to translate the Self-Compassion Scale' -- no fee, no non-commercial clause, no permission-required and no no-redistribution term, so nothing reserved and nothing to block on. Deposit itself is CC BY 4.0. Deviations from literal transcription: PDF line wrapping collapsed to single spaces; the instrument heading is prepended to the instruction sentence in `instructions`. See notes_moe2025_scs.csv for the SCS25_pre data anomaly and the instructions-translation divergence.
public_note: SCS25_pre's published responses were wrong until irw#2146: the source .sav's raw SCS25_pre column is not item 25 (it disagrees with its own reverse-scored twin for 66 of 95 respondents, and the author's SelfCompassion composite is built from the twin). The response table was rebuilt with SCS25_pre = 6 - SCS25_pre_rev; copies of moe2025_scs fetched before that release carry the old values. The item text itself is unaffected.
